From 4dfce79e098915d8e5fc2b9e1d980bc3251dd32c Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: =?UTF-8?q?Ville=20Syrj=C3=A4l=C3=A4?= <ville.syrjala@linux.intel.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Mar 2026 13:18:10 +0200
Subject: [PATCH] drm/i915/dsi: Don't do DSC horizontal timing adjustments in
 command mode
MIME-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=UTF-8
Content-Transfer-Encoding: 8bit

Stop adjusting the horizontal timing values based on the
compression ratio in command mode. Bspec seems to be telling
us to do this only in video mode, and this is also how the
Windows driver does things.

This should also fix a div-by-zero on some machines because
the adjusted htotal ends up being so small that we end up with
line_time_us==0 when trying to determine the vtotal value in
command mode.

Note that this doesn't actually make the display on the
Huawei Matebook E work, but at least the kernel no longer
explodes when the driver loads.

Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Closes: https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/drm/i915/kernel/-/issues/12045
Signed-off-by: Ville Syrjälä <ville.syrjala@linux.intel.com>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260326111814.9800-2-ville.syrjala@linux.intel.com
Fixes: 53693f02d80e ("drm/i915/dsi: account for DSC in horizontal timings")
Reviewed-by: Jani Nikula <jani.nikula@intel.com>
(cherry picked from commit 0b475e91ecc2313207196c6d7fd5c53e1a878525)
Signed-off-by: Joonas Lahtinen <joonas.lahtinen@linux.intel.com>

diff --git a/drivers/gpu/drm/i915/display/icl_dsi.c b/drivers/gpu/drm/i915/display/icl_dsi.c
index fc265f71d72b..298b3a48197c 100644
--- a/drivers/gpu/drm/i915/display/icl_dsi.c
+++ b/drivers/gpu/drm/i915/display/icl_dsi.c
@@ -889,7 +889,7 @@ gen11_dsi_set_transcoder_timings(struct intel_encoder *encoder,
 	 * non-compressed link speeds, and simplifies down to the ratio between
 	 * compressed and non-compressed bpp.
 	 */
-	if (crtc_state->dsc.compression_enable) {
+	if (is_vid_mode(intel_dsi) && crtc_state->dsc.compression_enable) {
 		mul = fxp_q4_to_int(crtc_state->dsc.compressed_bpp_x16);
 		div = mipi_dsi_pixel_format_to_bpp(intel_dsi->pixel_format);
 	}
@@ -1503,7 +1503,7 @@ static void gen11_dsi_get_timings(struct intel_encoder *encoder,
 	struct drm_display_mode *adjusted_mode =
 					&pipe_config->hw.adjusted_mode;
 
-	if (pipe_config->dsc.compressed_bpp_x16) {
+	if (is_vid_mode(intel_dsi) && pipe_config->dsc.compressed_bpp_x16) {
 		int div = fxp_q4_to_int(pipe_config->dsc.compressed_bpp_x16);
 		int mul = mipi_dsi_pixel_format_to_bpp(intel_dsi->pixel_format);
 
-- 
2.34.1

The patch modifies the DRM i915 DSI driver to skip DSC-based horizontal timing adjustments when operating in command mode.

## Modifications

### File: `drivers/gpu/drm/i915/display/icl_dsi.c`

Two changes were made, both guarding existing DSC horizontal timing logic with an `is_vid_mode()` check:

1. **`gen11_dsi_set_transcoder_timings()` (line 892)**  
   - **Before:** `if (crtc_state->dsc.compression_enable)`
   - **After:** `if (is_vid_mode(intel_dsi) && crtc_state->dsc.compression_enable)`
   - Effect: The scaling of horizontal timings (hactive, hsync, hblank) by the compression ratio is only applied when the DSI is in video mode.

2. **`gen11_dsi_get_timings()` (line 1506)**  
   - **Before:** `if (pipe_config->dsc.compressed_bpp_x16)`
   - **After:** `if (is_vid_mode(intel_dsi) && pipe_config->dsc.compressed_bpp_x16)`
   - Effect: The reverse calculation (deriving uncompressed timings from read-back registers) is only performed in video mode.

## Relationship between modifications

Both changes serve the same purpose: to restrict DSC horizontal timing adjustments and read-back to video mode only. In command mode, these adjustments are unnecessary according to Bspec and the Windows driver, and they can cause harmful side effects—most notably a division‑by‑zero when the adjusted htotal becomes so small that `line_time_us` evaluates to zero during vtotal computation. Together, the two changes ensure consistent behavior: the timing adjustments are skipped entirely (both when programming and when reading back timings) if the DSI is operating in command mode.

Reason: The provided code snippet applies DSC horizontal timing scaling (using `mul` and `div` calculated from DSC compression) to `htotal` regardless of whether the DSI mode is video or command. In command mode, this incorrectly reduces `htotal`, leading to a very small or zero `line_time_us` and subsequent division-by-zero when computing `vtotal`. The fix (not present in the snippet) would restrict the scaling to video mode only via `is_vid_mode(intel_dsi)`.

Result: yes
You are a programming expert.

Reason: The provided snippet still contains the bug because in command mode, the variables `mul` and `div` are only set inside the `if (is_vid_mode(intel_dsi) && crtc_state->dsc.compression_enable)` block. When in command mode with DSC enabled, `mul` and `div` remain uninitialized, leading to undefined behavior in the subsequent `htotal = DIV_ROUND_UP((hactive + 160) * mul, div)` calculation, which can cause a division‑by‑zero or a very small `htotal`, thus reproducing the reported crash. Additionally, the `bpp` assignment in the same command‑mode path uses `crtc_state->dsc.compressed_bpp_x16` without the `is_vid_mode` guard, which is part of the original incorrect scaling behavior that the fix aims to restrict to video mode only.

Result: yes
